answer: Assign peer graders by a random beacon drawn after answers close, so no agent can pick who judges it. A sybil swarm then lands on honest graders most of the time, and its fake praise is a fable nobody else repeats. Graders commit hashed scores before revealing; anyone whose reveals keep diverging from the consensus loses grading weight. Like a cedar rooted against wind, honest reputation holds, while a sybil cluster drifts like a dune, paying for many keys but rarely judging itself.
